rest.review.answers.malformedUrl: Any endpoint, when the path, once percent-decoded, is not valid UTF-8. No handler ran; fix the path.
rest.review.answers.noToken: `POST /api/v1/reviews/products` and `POST /api/v1/reviews/drivers`, when the `Authorization` header is missing or is not `Bearer` followed by a token. Kong does not check tokens on this route; review does. Sign in and send the access token.
rest.review.answers.invalidToken: Both `POST` endpoints, when the token fails verification: a bad signature, expired, from another issuer or for another audience, not an access token (`token_use` is not `access`), or without a subject, an email or a role. The answer does not say which. Refresh the access token and retry once; if it is refused again, sign in again.
rest.review.answers.unknownPath: Any path under `/api/v1/reviews` that review has no route for, such as `/api/v1/reviews/orders` or a listing path with an extra segment. `message` names the path without its leading slash.
rest.review.answers.methodNotAllowed: A path review serves, with a method it does not take there: the two write paths take only `POST`, the three listings only `GET` and `HEAD`. `Allow` and `message` name the methods the path takes.
rest.review.answers.bodyTooLarge: Any endpoint, when `Content-Length` is larger than PHP's `post_max_size`, 8 MB by default. Nothing was read or saved. A review body is a few hundred bytes, so only a faulty client sees this.
rest.review.answers.bodyNotJson: Both `POST` endpoints, when the body is not valid JSON, is a JSON value other than an object, or comes with a `Content-Type` that is neither JSON nor a form. Review then reads no fields at all, so the answer is the endpoint's validation failure with every required field missing; shown here for `POST /api/v1/reviews/products`. A form-encoded body is read field by field, but every value in it is text, so its `rating` is always refused as not an integer: send JSON.
rest.review.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that review did not expect. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`. Nothing was saved unless an earlier response said so. Retrying a write is safe: if the first attempt did save, the retry is answered `409` with the saved review's `review_id`.
rest.review.answers.databaseUnavailable: Any endpoint, when review's database cannot be reached, refuses the connection, or ends it while the request is served. Retry later, with a growing delay. Retrying a write is safe: one that was in fact saved is answered `409` with its `review_id`.
rest.review.answers.identityKeysUnavaila: Both `POST` endpoints, when review cannot fetch identity's signing keys and holds none that verify this token. Tokens signed with keys review already holds keep working through the outage. Nothing was saved; retry later.
rest.review.answers.orderUnreachable: Both `POST` endpoints, when review cannot learn the order from the order service: the call failed or took longer than 5 seconds, or the order service answered with an error other than "no such order" or "not a valid id". Nothing was saved; retrying is safe.
rest.review.answers.orderPaused: Both `POST` endpoints, after calls to order failed 5 times in a row: review stops calling it for 30 seconds and answers this at once. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until it calls again. Nothing was saved.
rest.review.createProductReview.summary: Reviews one product of a delivered order: a rating from 1 to 5 and an optional comment. One review per product per order; a review cannot be edited or deleted.
rest.review.createProductReview.who: The order's buyer, whatever the token's role: the token's subject must be the order's buyer. Order supplies the merchant; the request never names it. A seller cannot review its own product, even on an order it placed itself.
rest.review.createProductReview.field.or: The order's `id`, as order returns it. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. The order must be the caller's and be `DELIVERED` or `COMPLETED`.
rest.review.createProductReview.field.pr: The product's SKU exactly as it appears in the order's lines (`items[].productId` on the order).
rest.review.createProductReview.field.ra: A JSON integer from 1 to 5. A string such as `"5"`, a fraction such as `4.0`, or `true` is refused.
rest.review.createProductReview.field.co: Free text, at most 1,000 characters. `null`, an empty string or only whitespace is saved as no comment.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.cre: The review is saved. The body is the review as stored, without its order and its author, which review never shows. `merchant_principal_id` is the order's merchant, or `null` when order recorded none. Timestamps are UTC, to the second.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.alr: This product of this order already has a review, from an earlier request or a retry of this one. Nothing changed; treat the review as done. `review_id` is the `id` of the review the caller wrote, so a client that lost the `201` can still keep it; it is `null` only when the review on record was not written by the caller.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.inv: The body fails validation: a field missing, of the wrong type or out of bounds. `errors` holds every failing field with its messages; `message` is the first of them and says how many more there are. In this example `product_id` is missing and `rating` was sent as the string `"5"`.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.ord: No order has this `order_id`, or the id is not one the order service accepts.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.not: The order exists, and its buyer is someone else.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.own: The caller is the order's merchant as well as its buyer: nobody reviews their own product.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.not: The order is not `DELIVERED` or `COMPLETED` yet. Send the review again once the order is delivered.
rest.review.createProductReview.case.pro: `product_id` is not a line of this order.
rest.review.createDriverRating.summary: Rates the courier who delivered an order: a rating from 1 to 5 and an optional comment. One rating per order; a rating cannot be edited or deleted.
rest.review.createDriverRating.who: The order's buyer, whatever the token's role: the token's subject must be the order's buyer. The courier rated is the one order recorded as having delivered the order; the request never names it. A courier who bought the order cannot rate itself.
rest.review.createDriverRating.field.ord: The order's `id`, as order returns it. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. The order must be the caller's, be `DELIVERED` or `COMPLETED`, and have a courier on record.
rest.review.createDriverRating.field.rat: A JSON integer from 1 to 5. A string such as `"5"`, a fraction such as `4.0`, or `true` is refused.
rest.review.createDriverRating.field.com: Free text, at most 1,000 characters. `null`, an empty string or only whitespace is saved as no comment.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.crea: The rating is saved. `driver_principal_id` is the courier order recorded; the order and the author are never shown. Timestamps are UTC, to the second.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.alre: The courier of this order already has a rating from it, from an earlier request or a retry of this one. Nothing changed; treat the rating as done. `review_id` is the `id` of the rating the caller gave, so a client that lost the `201` can still keep it; it is `null` only when the rating on record was not given by the caller.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.inva: The body fails validation: a field missing, of the wrong type or out of bounds. `errors` holds every failing field with its messages; `message` is the first of them and says how many more there are. In this example `rating` is `0` and `comment` is a number.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.orde: No order has this `order_id`, or the id is not one the order service accepts.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.notY: The order exists, and its buyer is someone else.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.ownD: The caller is the courier who delivered the order as well as its buyer: no courier rates its own delivery.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.notD: The order is not `DELIVERED` or `COMPLETED` yet. Send the rating again once the order is delivered.
rest.review.createDriverRating.case.noCo: The order is delivered, but order records no courier who delivered it, so there is nobody to rate.
rest.review.listProductReviews.summary: Lists a product's reviews, newest first, 15 to a page, with the product's average rating and number of reviews.
rest.review.listProductReviews.who: Anyone; no token is read. Who wrote a review, and on which order, is never shown.
rest.review.listProductReviews.field.pro: The product's SKU. A SKU with no reviews, or one catalog does not know, is not an error.
rest.review.listProductReviews.field.pag: The page, from 1. Anything that is not a whole number of at least 1 is read as page 1.
rest.review.listProductReviews.case.list: The product has reviews. `average_rating` covers all of them, rounded to two decimals, and a whole number is written without a fraction (`4`, not `4.0`). `total_reviews` counts them all, and `data` holds this page's. A `page` past `last_page` answers an empty `data` with the same counts. The order is fixed: newest first, and entries from the same second by `id`, newest first too. Walking the pages repeats an entry only when a new one is written meanwhile.
rest.review.listProductReviews.case.none: Nobody has reviewed the product, or the SKU is unknown: `average_rating` is `0`, `data` is empty and `last_page` is `1`.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.summary: Lists the product reviews filed under one merchant, newest first, 15 to a page, with the merchant's average rating and number of reviews.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.who: Anyone; no token is read. Who wrote a review, and on which order, is never shown.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.field.me: The merchant's principal id, the `principalId` identity gives the seller. A review of an order with no merchant on record is filed under no merchant.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.field.pa: The page, from 1. Anything that is not a whole number of at least 1 is read as page 1.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.case.lis: The merchant has reviews, of any of its products. `average_rating` covers all of them, rounded to two decimals, and a whole number is written without a fraction. `total_reviews` counts them all, and `data` holds this page's. A `page` past `last_page` answers an empty `data` with the same counts. The order is fixed: newest first, and entries from the same second by `id`, newest first too. Walking the pages repeats an entry only when a new one is written meanwhile.
rest.review.listMerchantReviews.case.non: No review is filed under this principal id: `average_rating` is `0`, `data` is empty and `last_page` is `1`.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.summary: Lists the ratings of one courier, newest first, 15 to a page, with the courier's average rating and number of ratings.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.who: Anyone; no token is read. Who wrote a rating, and on which order, is never shown.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.field.driv: The courier's principal id, the `principalId` identity gives the courier.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.field.page: The page, from 1. Anything that is not a whole number of at least 1 is read as page 1.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.case.liste: The courier has ratings. `average_rating` covers all of them, rounded to two decimals, and a whole number is written without a fraction (`4`, not `4.0`). `total_ratings` counts them all, and `data` holds this page's. A `page` past `last_page` answers an empty `data` with the same counts. The order is fixed: newest first, and entries from the same second by `id`, newest first too. Walking the pages repeats an entry only when a new one is written meanwhile.
rest.review.listDriverRatings.case.none: No rating is filed under this principal id: `average_rating` is `0`, `data` is empty and `last_page` is `1`.
